lease_lifetime_review.scope: Read-only static audit of final lazy optional-span input ReadLease candidate collection. Only this review artifact is written. No product changes, build, native/model execution, instrumentation or rerun.
lease_lifetime_review.implementation: prepare_invocation_bindings owns one initially disengaged optional<span<const uint32_t>> and its original clear-candidate ScopeGuard. Both existing prepare_command_bindings call sites pass it by reference. The helper engages it only in the existing native and non-borrowed input branch immediately before input_lease.

cases.reason: Collection returns a successful empty span for no ResourceEpisode or zero qualifying reads. Assignment engages optional regardless of span.empty(); all later native inputs reuse that valid empty result rather than recollecting.

No input loop means no optional check or collection; output representation, generated output projection, change detection and provider hook/seal logic are unchanged. Ordinary-operation inputs also never consume this native lookup table.

The existing native-handle/reference validity exception remains. With no episode collection succeeds with an empty span; input_lease returns nullptr for absent resources or invalid TensorView. Native type, handle and reference still independently set native_inputs, preserving original forced invalidation. No borrowed TensorView is promoted into an owner.

Borrowed-only steps assign value.lease=nullptr without engaging optional. The first real non-borrowed native input collects all current eligible owned reads, in original binding order. Later native inputs use the same span; the preparation guard excludes public mutation of ResourceEpisode bindings for its lifetime. Generated projections change readable/native_values/bound, not the candidate backing vector or resource bindings.

The same input_lease lookup still skips exclusive reads, checks exact resource/native handle and contained byte interval, and returns the first covering owned read. All ordinary completeness, alignment, physical identity, revision/native invalidation and provider preparation checks remain. Submission still admits every current permission via the original LeaseUseBatch/LeasePermissionSet; optional span stores indices, grants no permission and retains no owner.

Once collection can occur, the outer clear ScopeGuard already exists. Capacity/guard failure during collect, invalid later input/output, provider prepare failure, generated projection failure and seal failure all unwind through it. The collector clears before checking capacity, so even a partial/rejected collection leaves no candidate tail. Success also clears. Earlier incomplete-binding exits cannot have collected, and bindings_prepared fast path cannot observe a table retained from a prior call because all such calls cleared on exit.

There is no added outer scan/lambda querying every region. The current helper reuses its already-computed borrowed_tensor_carrier and existing native branch. New runtime work is only optional engagement/check at actual non-borrowed native lookups; all-borrowed and zero-consumer preparations avoid the binding-vector collection entirely. No field, public API or cross-episode cache was added.
